messages:
alex: heads-up — AcmePayments (private VPC) is seeing intermittent 502s and streaming resets from our private inference endpoint. Happens mostly when responses are ~>2k tokens, roughly every 30–90s. I captured some client-side curl traces.

maria: private or dedicated? any NAT in path?

alex: private, routed through customer's NAT gateway + edge firewall. they use a tight NACL that they believe only allows ephemeral 32768-61000, but we see mappings above that sometimes. also TLS handshake looks fine, cert OK.

support-bot: ticket created INC-1456 — linking logs and customer traces.

sam: can you grab a tcpdump on the NAT/edge when it happens? need to see source port mapping and whether return packets are denied by NACL. example: `sudo tcpdump -nn -i eth0 host 10.1.2.3 and port 443` (capture both client and our inference egress IP).

alex: attached pcap in ticket. quick excerpt: client src 10.1.2.3:54872 -> our egress 34.55.66.77:443, NAT SNAT -> 3.4.5.6:62012. reply comes back to 3.4.5.6:62012 but NACL denies it.

irene: interesting — if their NACL ranges cap at 32767, anything SNATed into >32767 will be dropped. NAT gateways can allocate ephemeral ports outside the client's original ephemeral range. we should confirm their NACL rules. ask them to run: 
```
aws ec2 describe-network-acls --network-acl-ids acl-0abc123
```
and paste the entries.

maria: also ask customer for `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` on any linux NAT/edge devices — sometimes iptables masq port pools are different.

alex: customer pasted NACL entries; excerpt shows rule 100 ALLOW TCP 1024-32767, explicit DENY for 32768-65535 (rule 200). so yep — anything SNATed above 32767 is being dropped at the subnet boundary.

sam: that matches. root cause = NAT port allocation (our managed NAT or customer's NAT) selects high source ports for outbound connections; NACL prevents replies for those ports. quick repro: on a box behind same NACL, do `curl -v --local-port 62012 https://api.redwood.example/stream` and you'll see SYN then no response (RST) from NACL.

alex: ran that repro. output: 
```
* Connected to api.redwood.example (34.55.66.77) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.example left intact
```
then connection reset after TLS partial handshake when payload larger.

oncall-agent: check conntrack counts on NAT host: `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` and `ss -s` — port exhaustion or aggressive reuse can make time windows where mapping uses unexpected ports. Also check NAT gateway logs if available.

irene: mitigation options: 
- short-term: widen NACL ephemeral range to at least 1024-65535 or to the RFC 49152-65535 recommended range depending on policy. This will immediately stop drops.
- medium: configure NAT port allocation to a narrower range that matches the NACL (if you control the NAT host) via iptables `--random` and MASQUERADE port range or use `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` to restrict local ephemeral ports.
- long-term: move inference egress to a dedicated EIP and update SG/NACL to allow the ORIGIN EIP's port behavior (but widening NACL is simpler).

maria: steps I asked the customer to do: 
1) temporarily update NACL rule to ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 for outbound/inbound return path and test (no infra downtime required for NACL update).
2) run the curl repro and sample app load for 10 minutes and send pcap + `ss -s` if problem persists.

alex: customer applied change to NACL to allow 1024-65535, retried streaming load for 20 minutes — no 502s, no resets. they reverted change to confirm repro and re-applied. solid.

sam: note for internal runbook: when troubleshooting private inference resets, check NAT SNAT port mapping vs NACL allowed ephemeral range. typical failure mode = return packet denied because NACL blocks SNAT-assigned high port.

irene: added suggested cli snippets for customers to INC-1456. snippet to inspect NACL: 
```
aws ec2 describe-network-acls --network-acl-ids acl-0abc123 --query 'NetworkAcls[].Entries[]' --output json
```

and quick conntrack check: `sudo conntrack -L | grep 34.55.66.77 | wc -l`

alex: leaving follow-up to customer success to schedule a config review with AcmePayments. closing action: CS to recommend either NACL widening or NAT port-range clamp plus scheduled maintenance to avoid surprises. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: INC-1456 status -> triaged -> assigned to CS (maria)

maria: I'll own the postmortem and send the recommended config doc to the customer today. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
